key_insight: A differentiable foundation model jointly optimizes crystal composition and structure to design semiconductor candidates with band gaps near a photovoltaic target.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate solar-absorber materials discovery by optimizing electronic properties and energetic stability together.
method: DEFEAT enables a pretrained EquiformerV3 model to accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Property gradients and a learned energy penalty jointly update composition, atom count, positions, and lattice vectors.
SCAN calculations evaluate band gaps, while DFT hull comparisons assess candidate stability.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel crystal structures with gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; computed candidates are not experimentally validated solar cells.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
